sections.h2: Where is the Watauga County Register of Deeds in Boone?
sections.html:
The Watauga County Register of Deeds is in the county courthouse, Room 119, at 842 West King Street in Boone. The mailing address is the same street, Suite 9, Boone, NC 28607. The county contact page lists 828-265-8052 for land records and 828-265-8034 for vital records, with a fax at 828-265-7632.

Watauga County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of northwestern North Carolina. It was formed in 1849 from parts of Ashe, Caldwell, Wilkes and Yancey counties and named for the Watauga River. Boone is the county seat and the home of Appalachian State University, and the Blue Ridge Parkway runs through the county.

The register of deeds is elected by the county's voters under G.S. 161-1. Wills are not filed here. The county says wills go to the clerk of court, and that liens and judgments on real property are checked with the clerk of superior court.

sections.h2: What land records does the Watauga County office hold?
sections.html:
Indexes and images of land records since 1872 are on the county site, searchable by name or by book and page. Documents recorded before February 22, 1985 are in separate old index books, because on that date deeds and deeds of trust were merged into a single Book of Records starting at Book 1.

Recorded plats can be searched by book and page, by subdivision, or by the owner's name as grantor, whatever the recording date. State indexing standards took effect in 1995, and the office keeps copies of them.

All records filed with the office are public, with one exception the county names: military discharges filed less than 80 years ago. To find the owner of a particular parcel, the county FAQ sends callers to the tax mapping department at 828-265-8030.

sections.h2: What are the Watauga County recording fees?
sections.html:
A deed or general instrument costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 for each added page, and a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 per added page. The county's schedule says it was revised October 1, 2016, and it follows G.S. 161-10.

Watauga County fee schedule items as printed on the county page
ItemFee printed
Deed or instrument$26.00 first 15 pages, $4.00 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page
Record of satisfactionNo fee
Non-standard document$25.00 added to the filing fee
More than 20 distinct parties$2.00 per party over 20
Multiple instruments$10.00 for each added instrument
Plat$21.00 per sheet or page
Other certified copies$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Excise stamps$1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the value

The county notes that plats offered for registration must be 18 by 24 inches under a 1983 commissioner ordinance. Records furnished to help a person obtain veterans' benefits carry no charge.

sections.h2: Can I e-record a deed in Watauga County?
sections.html:
Yes. The register accepts electronic recording for all land record document types, and the county says it has over 1,500 e-recording submitters, including banks, attorney offices and mortgage companies.

The county lists three vendors that route documents to the office:

  • Simplifile, at 1-800-460-5657.
  • Corporation Service Company, at 1-866-652-0111.
  • eRecording Partners Network, at 1-888-325-3365.

Most home sales reach the office this way through the closing attorney, so a seller rarely carries paper to the counter. The county lists deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, easements and powers of attorney among the documents sent electronically.

sections.h2: What other services does the Watauga County Register of Deeds offer a homeowner?
sections.html:
Beyond land records, the office issues marriage licenses at $60.00 and certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates at $10.00, according to the county fee schedule. It also swears in notaries for a $10.00 oath fee, with $2.00 for verification of a commission, and keeps military discharge records.

The county menu also lists an assumed business name certificate, a public records redaction request form, a fraud notification system and an identity theft page. For a seller, the fraud notification system and the redaction request are the two worth knowing, because deeds and deeds of trust are public and can carry personal data.

  • Uncertified copies are priced as posted at the office.
  • A comparison of a copy for certification costs $5.00.
  • No fee applies to a certified copy of an armed forces discharge.

Call the vital records line at 828-265-8034 for birth and death certificates, and the land records line for anything tied to a deed.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Watauga County deed?
sections.html:
The seller pays. State law requires the transferor to pay the excise tax to the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded, at one dollar per $500 or fractional part of the consideration or value of the interest.

Half of that money stays with the county and half goes to the Department of Revenue, per G.S. 105-228.30. The closing attorney calculates the stamp and shows it on the settlement statement.

North Carolina has no state estate tax for deaths on or after January 1, 2013, since the statutes were repealed, so an inherited Watauga County house does not add an estate tax step to the recording.

sections.h2: Do I have to record a deed in Watauga County, and who can draft it?
sections.html:
Recording is not optional in practice. The county says a deed should be recorded as soon as possible after it is drawn, because failing to record can make a later transfer or mortgage impossible to prove. State law is the reason: under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies.

The county says an owner may draft a deed, but it strongly recommends an attorney. To add or remove a name, a new deed must be drawn and filed, and forms are not available at the register's office.

A title search through the register's index shows how the current owner took title, which matters when ownership passed through heirs or a trust.

sections.h2: What does a seller do if the Watauga County deed has problems?
sections.html:
Start with the index. Search the owner's name in the land records, note the book and page of the last deed, and check for open deeds of trust that lack a recorded satisfaction. Satisfactions cost nothing to record.

Then call the clerk of superior court about liens and judgments, and the tax office about the account. A house with defects can still be sold as-is. If you want to weigh a cash offer on a Watauga County house against a listing, you can request one from this site.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Watauga County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: In the courthouse, Room 119, 842 West King Street in Boone. Land records calls go to 828-265-8052 and vital records calls to 828-265-8034.

faqs.q: How far back are Watauga County land records online?
faqs.a: Indexes and images go back to 1872, and records from before February 22, 1985 are found under the old index books tab.

faqs.q: Does Watauga County charge to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. The county's schedule lists records of satisfaction as no fee.

faqs.q: Are wills filed at the Watauga County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: No. The county says wills are filed with the clerk of courts. Separation agreements can be obtained from the register, but divorces are filed with the clerk.

faqs.q: Can I record a Watauga County deed electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, through the e-recording vendors the county lists, which are Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and eRecording Partners Network. Most sellers go through their closing attorney.
